prompt: Moving from node A to its connected node B, one hop:

options.label: With an index lookup
options.content: The engine has to search an index (or scan a table) to find which row(s) reference A's ID as a match. Even a fast, well-tuned index is still performing a real lookup operation - and that same lookup cost repeats at every single additional hop in a longer traversal.

options.label: Index-free adjacency
options.content: Node A already physically stores a direct pointer to node B - moving to B is just following that reference, no search involved at all. This is the same underlying idea as a linked list's `next` pointer: the connection was never something to be found, it was already sitting there the moment you arrived at A.
